summary: Argentina is in a quieter stretch under President Milei, but stocks are slipping. The Merval fell 1% to 94,530 on Oct 29, its fourth straight loss, while dollar bonds bounced and country risk eased back under 750 points (Ambito, Infobae). That is still above the 709 seen on Oct 22, so the trend in risk is up. Monthly inflation was 1.9% in September and yearly inflation 33.4%, and the IMF's third review is still open. Energy names ride Vaca Muerta output and oil above $100.
for_you: Argentina is a high risk, high swing market. YPF and VIST ride oil above $100. Keep any trade small, and check the inflation print on Oct 13 first.

watch.name: Pesos per US dollar (official)
watch.why: A nominal record at Banco Nacion; the wholesale rate was 1,528 (Ambito via Rio Times).

watch.name: Central bank reserves
watch.why: Rising reserves back the peso and the ability to pay dollar bonds.

watch.name: Monthly inflation (INDEC)
watch.why: September reading, released Oct 13; in line with the 1.9% survey forecast. Yearly rate 33.4%.

watch.name: IMF third review
watch.why: A completed review releases funds and calms bond markets.

watch.name: Country risk
watch.why: Bonds rebounded and the spread eased back under 750 points (Ambito); up from 709 on Oct 22.

exposed.name: YPF
exposed.exposure: state controlled oil and gas company, nearly all assets in Argentina (company filings)
exposed.how: Biggest Vaca Muerta producer, so high oil prices and export growth help it; peso and policy moves swing the stock.

exposed.name: Vista Energy
exposed.exposure: nearly all production in Vaca Muerta, Argentina (company filings)
exposed.how: Pure Vaca Muerta oil producer that sells much of its oil for export, so Brent above $100 helps.

exposed.name: Grupo Financiero Galicia
exposed.exposure: Argentine bank holding company, nearly all business in Argentina (company filings)
exposed.how: Falling inflation and lower rates grow lending but squeeze margins; it trades on confidence in the Milei program.

exposed.name: Banco Macro
exposed.exposure: Argentine bank, nearly all business in Argentina (company filings)
exposed.how: Same drivers as Galicia: inflation, rates and the IMF review.

exposed.name: Pampa Energia
exposed.exposure: Argentine power and gas company, nearly all assets in Argentina (company filings)
exposed.how: Gains from gas output and regulated tariff increases as subsidies are cut.

exposed.name: Transportadora de Gas del Sur
exposed.exposure: Argentine gas pipeline company, nearly all assets in Argentina (company filings)
exposed.how: Carries Vaca Muerta gas; benefits from higher regulated tariffs and new pipeline capacity.

exposed.name: MercadoLibre
exposed.exposure: about 21% of 2025 net revenue from Argentina ($6.0 billion of $28.9 billion, FY2025 10-K segment data)
exposed.how: Argentina is its home market; a stable peso and falling inflation help reported growth.

changes.what: An IMF mission to Buenos Aires ended Sep 29 without closing the third program review. Reserves near $48.7 billion and a peso well inside its band support the case, but the review is still pending.

INDEC said September prices rose 1.9% in the month, in line with the 1.9% forecast and up from 1.7% in August. Yearly inflation is 33.4% and prices are up 23.6% in 2026. Housing, water, power and fuel rose most, 3.1%, as subsidies keep falling.
changes.for_you: No action. An in line print removes one risk for GGAL and BMA but gives them no new push, so they are left out of both lists. Higher regulated utility prices help PAM and TGS a little. YPF still trades on oil.

changes.what: Pampa Energia director and 10% owner Marcos Mindlin bought about $35.1 million of PAM ADRs at $80.78 on Oct 15 (filed Oct 16), on top of buys by two vice presidents in late September; the insider cluster is about $42.7 million. PAM closed at 81.10 on Oct 16, up 0.8% (dashboard).
changes.for_you: Research only: PAM has no dashboard verdict. A controlling shareholder buying $35 million in the open market is the strongest kind of insider signal; if PAM gets a verdict, check whether the chart is ready before acting.

changes.what: Argentina's country risk rose to 709 points on Oct 22 and the official dollar sold at a nominal record 1,550 pesos at Banco Nacion (wholesale 1,528), while the Merval fell 1.5% to 97,993 as the tech sell off hit ADRs (Rio Times).
changes.for_you: No action. No Argentine stock is on the buy zone list. Bank ADRs suffer first when the peso slides; energy names like YPF and PAM earn in dollars and are left out of the bearish list.

changes.what: The Merval fell 1% to 94,530 on Oct 29, a fourth straight loss, while dollar bonds rebounded and country risk eased under 750 points (Ambito). In New York YPF fell 3.10% to 47.81 and ARGT 1.03% to 81.48 (Massive).
changes.for_you: No action. No Argentine stock is on the buy zone list; YPF tracks oil more than Buenos Aires.
